title: redirect()/revalidatePath() still run inside the tenant scope body, and nothing states or enforces the invariant (REVIEW-FINDINGS #16)
why_open: The invariant does not exist in any form. apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:409-418 (`withTenantScope`) and apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:84-89 (`runInTenantScope`) run the caller's callback and say nothing about Next.js control-flow throws; grep for NEXT_REDIRECT/isRedirectError/unstable_rethrow across apps, packages, tests and tools returns only apps/system-studio/src/app/signin/page.tsx:66 and apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.test.ts:258. That test is the proof the codebase encodes the OPPOSITE rule: 'lets the body's error out unchanged' (tenant-scope.test.ts:247-261) deliberately asserts a NEXT_REDIRECT propagates out of the scope. A lexical scan of every `withTenantScope(` callback body finds 66 redirect/revalidatePath calls inside the scope, 9 of them real `redirect()` throws: apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/actions.ts:135, :190, :224, :255, :319; apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/actions.ts:168; apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/actions.ts:73; apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/documents/actions.ts:113, :214; apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:490. messages/actions.ts:102-126 is a `db.$transaction` immediately followed by the redirect at :135 — one edit moving that redirect inside the transaction callback silently rolls the whole conversation+message+delivery write back while the browser navigates as though it succeeded, and nothing in the repo would fail. (approvals/actions.ts:181-182 has the same shape and is EXCLUDED — another run owns that directory.) On the cache() half of #16: apps/web/src/lib/rbac.ts:42 `getUserContext` is React.cache()d and returns InstitutionMembership rows (a TENANT_SCOPED model, registry.ts:30) for every institution the user belongs to, and it is consulted inside tenant scopes at apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:26-27 and apps/web/src/lib/messaging.ts:38-41; no test or comment anywhere states 'no cache()d function may return tenant rows'.
smallest_real_change: (1) New tests/architecture/redirect-outside-tenant-scope.test.mjs: parse every apps/web/src/app/**/actions.ts, find each `withTenantScope(`/`runInTenantScope(`/`withSystemTenantScope(` callback by brace/paren matching, and FAIL naming file:line for any `redirect(`, `revalidatePath(` or `revalidateTag(` inside it. Seed it with exactly one documented exception — apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts, owned by a concurrent change — recorded as a named known-open entry, never as a widened pattern. (2) Move the 8 non-approvals `redirect()` calls out: have the scope body RETURN the target (`const href = await withTenantScope(userId, async () => { ...; return `/messages/${convo.id}` }); redirect(href)`), and lift the revalidatePath calls in the same files to after the scope closes. (3) Rewrite tenant-scope.test.ts:247-261 so it still proves errors propagate (throw a plain Error) instead of blessing NEXT_REDIRECT, and add a positive test that the returned-href shape survives. (4) State the cache() invariant where it binds: a doc block on apps/web/src/lib/rbac.ts:42 plus an assertion in the same architecture test that no `= cache(` wrapper under apps/web/src/lib takes zero arguments while querying a TENANT_SCOPED model from registry.ts. Mutation proof: move messages/actions.ts's `redirect(`/messages/${convo.id}`)` back inside the withTenantScope callback -> the scanner test must FAIL naming messages/actions.ts and that line; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: delete `revalidatePath` from the scanned token list -> the calendar/actions.ts case must stop being caught, proving the list is load-bearing. Run `npm run test:platform` and `npm run test --workspace apps/web -- --ci` after; the e2e suite (Postgres is up per docker ps) covers /messages compose and /calendar new, both of which are on the changed path.

title: Adversarial external id: /api/attachment/[id] reads another tenant's attachment with no tenant scope and an institution-blind ACL
why_open: apps/web/src/app/api/attachment/[id]/route.ts:22 does `db.attachment.findUnique({ where: { id } })` with no `withTenantScope` anywhere in the file (imports at :1-6), and apps/web/src/app/api/attachment/[id]/content/route.ts has the same shape — they are 2 of only 10 API routes with no scope at all. The chokepoint cannot save them even with TENANCY_ENFORCE=true (set in infrastructure/terraform/ecs.tf:191 and .github/workflows/ci.yml:322): Attachment is listed UNENFORCEABLE at apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/registry.ts:83, so apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/scope-args.ts:65-70 returns `pass-through` and no predicate is added. The only gate left is apps/web/src/lib/messaging.ts:37-41, whose OSE_BROADCAST arm is `isOse(ctx, convo.institutionId) || ctx.orgRoles.some(r => r.status === 'ACTIVE' || r.status === 'SHADOW')` — the second clause never compares the reader's institution to `convo.institutionId`, and it cannot, because OrgRole (apps/web/src/lib/rbac.ts:12-26) carries no institutionId. Every other arm IS bound (BOARD_CHANNEL matches organizationId at :35, APPROVAL_THREAD/DIRECT_MESSAGE match participants), which isolates this as the one hole. So a signed-in user at institution A holding any ACTIVE/SHADOW seat downloads institution B's broadcast attachment from a guessed id — precisely the adversarial-external-id case this requirement exists to disprove. apps/web/src/lib/messaging.test.ts uses a single institution constant throughout and asserts no cross-institution denial.
smallest_real_change: Give `canReadConversation` the acting institution instead of letting it infer one: change the signature to `canReadConversation(ctx, convo, actingInstitutionId)` and make the FIRST line `if (convo.institutionId !== actingInstitutionId) return false` — a single early return that binds every arm, not just OSE_BROADCAST, and needs no schema change. Then wrap both attachment routes in `withTenantScope(userId, async (scope) => ...)` and pass `scope.institutionId`; the participant short-circuit at messaging.ts:32 must move BELOW the new check, otherwise a cross-tenant participant row still passes. Fix the two other call sites the compiler will name (grep `canReadConversation` — messaging-data.ts and the messages routes) in the same change, since adding a required third parameter is exactly the widening that breaks consumers silently if it is made optional. Tests in messaging.test.ts: build a conversation at inst_b, a ctx whose only orgRole is ACTIVE at an inst_a club, assert `false` for OSE_BROADCAST, BOARD_CHANNEL, APPROVAL_THREAD and DIRECT_MESSAGE-with-participant. Mutation proof: delete the `convo.institutionId !== actingInstitutionId` line -> all four assertions must FAIL; restore -> PASS. Second mutation on the producer, not the helper: in apps/web/src/app/api/attachment/[id]/route.ts pass a hardcoded `convo.institutionId` instead of `scope.institutionId` -> the route-level itest must FAIL. Add the end-to-end case to apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/isolation.itest.ts (Postgres is running) so the proof is against the real database and the real route, not only the pure helper.

title: The outbound delivery primitive has producers but no consumer: nothing drains OutboxEvent
why_open: This got WORSE recently, not better. Rows are now genuinely written — apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:154-155 creates one inside the approval transaction and :436-437 creates another — but nothing on the platform ever reads one for delivery. apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts:86-106 declares `OutboxPorts` and :140 `dispatchOnce`, :212 `replay`, and grep for `dispatchOnce|OutboxPorts|from "@/lib/outbox` across apps/web/src returns only the definitions and apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.test.ts, which exercises them against hand-written fakes. `ls apps/web/src/lib/outbox` is exactly two files: outbox.ts and outbox.test.ts — there is no Prisma adapter. `ls apps/web/src/app/api/jobs` is exactly one directory, `reminders` — there is no runner. The only other reference to the table in the whole app is a read for offboarding at apps/web/src/lib/platform/tenant-export.ts:74. So the queue accumulates a row per approval decision forever, `backoffMs`/MAX_ATTEMPTS/dead-lettering/`replay` are unreachable code, and the ledger's own words for this class of defect — 'watching a queue nothing can write to' — now invert into a queue nothing can read. apps/web/src/lib/jobs/ contains only reminders-isolation.itest.ts, no job module at all.
smallest_real_change: (1) New apps/web/src/lib/outbox/prisma-ports.ts implementing `OutboxPorts` over `db.outboxEvent`. `claimDue` MUST be one atomic statement — `db.$queryRaw` doing `UPDATE "OutboxEvent" SET state='dispatching', attempts=attempts+1 WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM "OutboxEvent" WHERE state='pending' AND "availableAt" <= $now ORDER BY "availableAt" FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT $n) RETURNING *` — because outbox.ts:88-93 states the contract as atomic and a findMany+updateMany pair lets two runners claim the same row, turning bounded at-least-once into unbounded. markDispatched/scheduleRetry/deadLetter/listDead/requeue map straight onto the existing columns. (2) New apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts modelled line-for-line on apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts: same bearer-token guard, same `parseJobRequest` envelope, and `forEachInstitution('outbox-dispatch', ...)` from @/lib/tenant-scope so each pass runs inside one tenant's scope (OutboxEvent is TENANT_SCOPED at registry.ts:28, so a cross-tenant drain would throw under TENANCY_ENFORCE=true — that is the correct shape, not an obstacle). `deliver` starts as the in-process notifier the approvals path already calls inline, so the route does real work on day one rather than shipping a port with no implementation. (3) prisma-ports.test.ts against an in-memory fake that enforces the real semantics (unique eventId; a claim only matches rows still `pending`), asserting two concurrent claimDue calls cannot both return the same row. Mutation proof on the producer path, not the helper: change claimDue to a plain findMany with no state flip -> the concurrency assertion must FAIL; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: point `deliver` at a port that always throws and assert the row reaches state 'dead' after MAX_ATTEMPTS rather than being retried forever. (4) apps/web/src/lib/jobs/outbox-dispatch.itest.ts against the running Postgres: write an approval decision, run the route handler, assert the row moved pending->dispatched and that a second run claims nothing.

title: Relay answers are neither citation-verified nor current: SearchDoc carries no timestamp and the model's answer is returned unchecked
why_open: 'cited' and 'current enough' are both unimplementable against the present types. apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:7-14 `SearchDoc` is `{ id, kind, title, body, href, context }` — there is no `occurredAt`/`updatedAt`/`asOf` field anywhere on it, and apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:51-70 never selects one from any of the four queries, so nothing downstream can say how old a retrieved passage is or refuse a stale one. On citations: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:133-140 instructs the model to 'Cite every claim with its source number in brackets' and then returns `answer` verbatim at :144 with no post-hoc check that the bracketed numbers exist in the offered set — an answer citing [7] against 6 sources, or citing nothing at all, is shipped to the user as a grounded answer. `sources` at :103-108 is projected as title/href/kind/context only, so even the client cannot show recency. This is the gate's whole subject and every clause of it is currently a prompt string rather than a control.
smallest_real_change: (1) Add a required `asOf: Date` to `SearchDoc` (apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:7) — REQUIRED, not optional, so `tsc` names every construction site instead of letting an unset field fail at runtime; the sites are the five builders in apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts (memory/document/approval/event/organization), and each already has a timestamp column to select (`updatedAt` on MemoryRecord/Document/Organization, `createdAt` on ApprovalRequest, `startsAt` on Event). Grep `SearchDoc` and `ScoredDoc` before landing and fix every one in the same change. (2) New exported `verifyCitations(answer: string, sourceCount: number): { cited: number[]; invalid: number[] }` in search.ts, and in chat/route.ts:141 refuse to return an answer whose `invalid` list is non-empty — replace it with the sources-only response the route already produces when no key is configured, and report the reason in the existing `toolRefusal`-style field. That is the smallest change that makes 'cited' a property of the response rather than of the prompt. (3) Project `asOf` into the `sources` array at route.ts:103-108 so the client can render recency. Tests in search.test.ts: `verifyCitations('per [1] and [7]', 6)` returns invalid [7]; `verifyCitations('no citations here', 6)` returns cited []. Mutation proof on the PRODUCER: in chat/route.ts change the guard to return the answer regardless of `invalid` -> the route test asserting a fabricated-citation answer is suppressed must FAIL; restore -> PASS. Do not prove this by calling verifyCitations directly, or the test stays green when the route stops calling it. Second mutation: drop `asOf` from the document builder in search-data.ts -> `tsc` must fail, which is the point of making the field required.

title: There is one tool class, not five: `readOnly` is declared on the only registration in the platform and read by nothing
why_open: The taxonomy this requires (read / draft / write / sync / admin, each with a schema and a policy) does not exist. The contract carries a single boolean: packages/contracts/src/index.ts:711-719 `ToolRegistration` is `{ toolKey, module, description, requiredPermission, readOnly, reauthorizesPerCall }` and there is no input/output schema field at all, so a tool's arguments are unvalidated by construction. There is exactly ONE registration on the whole platform — `grep -c toolKey modules/index.ts` returns 1 — modules/index.ts:464-473, `search.corpus`, `readOnly: true`. And `readOnly` is never consulted: grep across apps/web/src, modules and packages/platform-config finds it only in prose (apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:33 and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:46 are comments, modules/index.ts:471 is the declaration). apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:101-123 authorizes every tool identically on `requiredPermission` alone, so the moment a second, writing registration is added it is handed to the model on the same footing as a read — via a question-answering route (chat/route.ts:99-100) that has no confirmation, preview or step-up step of any kind.
smallest_real_change: Do NOT edit packages/contracts/src/index.ts — a concurrent run owns it, so the five-class enum on `ToolRegistration` cannot land in this change and that half must be reported honestly as blocked on that file. What IS fully implementable here, and closes the reachable hole: make `readOnly` load-bearing in apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts. Add a required `allow: 'read-only' | 'any'` parameter to `authorizeRelayTools` (required, so `tsc` names both call sites — chat/route.ts:99 and relay-tools.test.ts — rather than letting an unset option default silently), and when `allow` is 'read-only' refuse every registration with `readOnly === false` BEFORE the permission check, pushing it onto `refused` with reason 'this surface offers read tools only; <toolKey> writes'. Pass 'read-only' from apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:99, because that route has no confirmation or receipt step and therefore cannot legitimately offer a writing tool. Test in relay-tools.test.ts with a stub module catalog containing one readOnly:true and one readOnly:false registration: assert the writing one appears in `refused` with that reason and never in `offered`. Mutation proof on the producer: change chat/route.ts to pass 'any' -> the route-level test asserting the writing tool is not offered must FAIL; restore -> PASS. That mutation is on the caller, not on authorizeRelayTools, so it stays honest if the route later stops passing the flag.

title: Nothing binds retrieval to a purpose, and the model-exposure decision records no policy revision
why_open: Two of the three clauses ('current Tenure ... purpose/policy authorization') have no representation in the code. (a) Purpose: apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:13-28 `TenantScope` is `{ institutionId, actor }` — there is no `purpose` field, and grep for `purpose` across apps/web/src/lib/tenancy returns nothing. docs/architecture/REVIEW-FINDINGS.md:19 records that one of the two competing designs was `withTenant({ tenantId, purpose }, fn)`; the surviving implementation dropped the purpose and nobody noticed, so a scope opened to render a calendar page and a scope opened to feed a third-party model are indistinguishable to the query layer. (b) Policy revision: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:89-97 builds the TenantContext the exposure decision rests on with `configRevision` but no `policyRevision`, even though apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/request-context.ts:51 declares `policyRevision` as a required field of RequestContext — and `runWithContext`/`requireContext`/`currentContext` (request-context.ts:148, :153, :164) have ZERO production callers (grep across apps/web/src excluding the module and its test returns nothing), so the type that would carry it is dead. The source-ACL clause IS implemented (apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:94 `authorizeRetrieved`, called from search-data.ts) — that is what isolates purpose and policy-revision as the open part.
smallest_real_change: Add a required `purpose` to `TenantScope` (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:13) as a closed union — 'interactive' | 'model-exposure' | 'job' | 'support' | 'export' — and thread it through the three constructors in apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts (`scopeForUser`:165, `withSystemTenantScope`:428, `forEachInstitution`:456). REQUIRED, not optional: an optional purpose that a caller never sets compiles, passes every unit test that builds its own fixture, and is invisible until the audit needs it. Grep `TenantScope` and `scopeForUser` and fix every construction site in the same change — the ones I found are tenant-scope.ts:165/433, platform/tenant-export.ts:132, and the fixtures in tenancy/*.test.ts. Then make it decide something rather than only being recorded: in apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts, `loadSearchCorpus` refuses to run unless `requireTenantScope('loadSearchCorpus').purpose === 'model-exposure'`, and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:69 opens its scope with that purpose while the /search page and /api/search open theirs as 'interactive' and call a sibling entry point. Mutation proof on the producer: change chat/route.ts to open the scope with purpose 'interactive' -> the route test asserting retrieval still works must FAIL with the refusal; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: make the field optional -> the context.test.ts case asserting `runInTenantScope` rejects a scope with no purpose must FAIL. Leave `policyRevision` alone in this change unless request-context.ts gains its first caller — adding a field to a type nothing constructs is the dead-code failure this bar forbids.

title: Capability resolution discloses tools the principal may not use, and hands the authorization engine's internal detail to the browser
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:66-71 `relayToolsFor` enumerates every registration the tenant's enabled modules contribute, with no reference to the principal; :99-125 then splits them into `offered` and `refused`, where each `RefusedTool` (:44-50) carries `toolKey`, `requiredPermission` and the authorization engine's own `decision.detail`. apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:151-154 returns that detail straight to the browser as `toolRefusal`. So the response tells an unprivileged caller that a capability exists here, names the exact permission key that would unlock it, and quotes the engine's reasoning — which is the disclosure of a hidden resource this requirement forbids, and the same 404-vs-deny-reason contradiction REVIEW-FINDINGS.md:71 flags. There is no distinction anywhere between 'this system does not have that capability' and 'you may not use it', even though the route's own comment at :43-45 argues those must not be collapsed. Today the blast radius is one read-only tool; the shape is what is wrong, and it is the shape every future connector capability will resolve through.
smallest_real_change: Split the refusal into a safe outcome and an internal one. In apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts give `RefusedTool` a `disclosure: 'not-in-this-system' | 'not-permitted'` and a `safeReason` string written for the person ('Search is not part of this system.' / 'You do not have access to search here.'), keeping `requiredPermission` and the engine `reason` on the object for logging only. Then change apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:151-154 to return `safeReason` and never `reason`/`requiredPermission`. Adding two required fields to `RefusedTool` makes `tsc` name every construction site (relay-tools.ts:117 and the test fixtures) rather than leaving an optional field unset at one of them. Test in relay-tools.test.ts: a principal lacking `search.index.query` in a tenant that HAS the search module gets disclosure 'not-permitted'; the same principal in a tenant whose blueprint omits search gets 'not-in-this-system'; and assert on the route's JSON body that no permission key and no engine detail string appears anywhere in it. Mutation proof on the producer: change chat/route.ts back to returning `r.reason` -> the route-body assertion must FAIL naming the leaked string; restore -> PASS.

title: The document graph records no binding between the WRK Bible and the eight authorities it defers to
why_open: The Bible states its bindings in prose — Tenure_Universal_Work_Graph_and_Workspace_Connector_Cloud_Claude_Bible_v1.0.md:30-34 names the Integration, Tenant UX, Configurator, Global System Architecture and owning-domain Bibles, and :49 states the ownership split ('The Integration Bible continues to own the shared connector SDK/runtime ... Domain Bibles own the meaning and invariants of Finance, HCM, ...'). The machine-readable graph carries none of it: docs/architecture/architecture-document-graph.yaml:506-520 is the WRK entry and its only relational fields are `superseded_by: null`, `supersedes: []`, `aliases: []` and `requirement_prefixes: [WRK]`. Scanning the whole file, no document has any binding, defers-to or owned-by edge — the schema does not have one. So nothing can detect that a WRK requirement was resolved against a Bible that has since been superseded, and tests/architecture/document-graph.test.mjs cannot assert a binding it has no field to read. This is one of the few WRK items that is entirely implementable now: it needs no provider, no AWS and no external decision.
smallest_real_change: Extend tools/document-graph.mjs to extract, per authority, the list of other authorities it names in its own binding section (the numbered list under the 'This Bible binds to' / 'Authorities' heading — for WRK, lines 28-34) and emit it as `binds: [<document id>, ...]` on each document entry, resolving each name to a canonical document id through the same family/alias table the generator already builds. Then add an assertion to tests/architecture/document-graph.test.mjs that (a) every id in every `binds` list resolves to a document present in the graph, and (b) no `binds` entry points at a document whose `superseded_by` is non-null — a requirement resolved against a retired authority is the failure this edge exists to catch. Regenerate the yaml with the generator (it is marked 'Do not edit by hand' at line 1) and record the evidence in the ledger entry for WRK-000-004. Mutation proof: change one name in the Bible's binding list to a Bible that does not exist in the repo -> the resolution assertion must FAIL naming that document; restore -> PASS. Second mutation: set `superseded_by` on one bound document in the generator's output -> the retired-authority assertion must FAIL. Both mutations are on the generated graph, which is what the ledger cites, not on a helper.
